# Setup
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(here)
library(tibble)
library(terra)
```

# DFO Fisheries Atlas Exporation

```{r inspect-fisheries-geodatabase}
# Define the location of the original fisheries geodatabase
fisheries_geodatabase_path <- here(
  "data",
  "raw_data",
  "DFO_FisheriesAtlas",
  "Maritimes_Fisheries_Atlas_2019_2023.gdb"
)

# Inspect available spatial layers
fisheries_layer_information <- st_layers(
  fisheries_geodatabase_path
)

# Create a tidy summary of available layers
fisheries_layer_summary <- tibble(
  layer_name = fisheries_layer_information$name,
  geometry_type = vapply(
    fisheries_layer_information$geomtype,
    paste,
    collapse = ", ",
    FUN.VALUE = character(1)
  ),
  feature_count = fisheries_layer_information$features
)

# Display all available layers
print(fisheries_layer_summary, n = Inf)
```

## Biological Data Inspection
Checking attribute names, consistency of data structure, data types, and confirming the records contain spatial features.

```{r inspect-biological-data}

# Identify the layers for species of interest:
selected_species_layers <- c(
  bluefin_tuna = "BluefinTuna_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  atlantic_herring = "Herring_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  atlantic_mackerel = "Mackerel_Landings_Weight_2019_2023",
  squid = "Squid_Landings_Weight_2019_2023"
)

# Import species datasets
fisheries_species_data <- lapply(
  selected_species_layers,
  function(layer_name) {
    st_read(
      dsn = fisheries_geodatabase_path,
      layer = layer_name,
      quiet = TRUE
    )
  }
)

# Inspect column names for each species
species_attribute_summary <- lapply(
  fisheries_species_data,
  names
)

species_attribute_summary

# Preview bluefin tuna records
head(fisheries_species_data$bluefin_tuna)

```

## Fisheries Data Validation

```{r validate-fisheries-data}

# Check spatial properties and missing values
fisheries_compatibility_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  fisheries_species_data,
  function(species_data, species_name) {

    geographic_extent <- st_bbox(
      st_transform(species_data, 4326)
    )

    tibble(
      species = species_name,
      feature_count = nrow(species_data),
      crs_epsg = st_crs(species_data)$epsg,
      geometry_type = paste(
        unique(as.character(st_geometry_type(species_data))),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      invalid_geometries = sum(!st_is_valid(species_data), na.rm = TRUE),
      missing_attribute_values = sum(
        is.na(st_drop_geometry(species_data))
      ),
      longitude_min = unname(geographic_extent["xmin"]),
      longitude_max = unname(geographic_extent["xmax"]),
      latitude_min = unname(geographic_extent["ymin"]),
      latitude_max = unname(geographic_extent["ymax"])
    )
  }
)

# Display spatial compatibility
print(fisheries_compatibility_summary, width = Inf)

# Inspect attribute names and data types
fisheries_attribute_summary <- purrr::imap_dfr(
  fisheries_species_data,
  function(species_data, species_name) {

    tibble(
      species = species_name,
      attribute_name = names(st_drop_geometry(species_data)),
      data_type = vapply(
        st_drop_geometry(species_data),
        function(attribute_values) {
          paste(class(attribute_values), collapse = ", ")
        },
        character(1)
      )
    )
  }
)

print(fisheries_attribute_summary, n = Inf)
```
Given that this is my core dataset I can define a preliminary bounding box for future environmental datasets.

```{r}
study_area_extent <- c(
  longitude_min = -68,
  longitude_max = -55,
  latitude_min = 39,
  latitude_max = 48
)
```

# GEBCO Exploration

```{r}
gebco_bathymetry <- rast(
  here("data", "raw_data", "GEBCO", "gebco_2026_n48.0_s39.0_w-68.0_e-55.0_geotiff.tif")
)

# Inspect spatial properties
gebco_spatial_summary <- tibble(
  dataset = "GEBCO 2026 Bathymetry",
  coordinate_reference_system = crs(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_min = xmin(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_max = xmax(gebco_bathymetry),
  latitude_min = ymin(gebco_bathymetry),
  latitude_max = ymax(gebco_bathymetry),
  longitude_resolution = res(gebco_bathymetry)[1],
  latitude_resolution = res(gebco_bathymetry)[2],
  raster_columns = ncol(gebco_bathymetry),
  raster_rows = nrow(gebco_bathymetry),
  missing_cells = global(is.na(gebco_bathymetry), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]
)

# Display spatial properties
print(gebco_spatial_summary, width = Inf)

# Inspect elevation and depth values
gebco_depth_summary <- global(
  gebco_bathymetry,
  fun = c("min", "max", "mean"),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

print(gebco_depth_summary)
```
The GEBCO dataset will work; it's got all four fisheries layers including geographic extents, it's got decent spatial resolution, and has no missing raster cells. 

# Copernicus Data Exploration

```{r inspect-copernicus-data}

# Identify the downloaded NetCDF file
copernicus_file_path <- list.files(
  here("data", "raw_data", "Copernicus"),
  pattern = "\\.nc$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

# Inspect available variables
copernicus_variables <- terra::sds(copernicus_file_path)

copernicus_variables
```

```{r validate-copernicus-time}

# Extract monthly timestamps from the temperature dataset
copernicus_temperature <- copernicus_variables["thetao"]

copernicus_time_summary <- tibble(
  first_observation = min(time(copernicus_temperature)),
  last_observation = max(time(copernicus_temperature)),
  number_of_months = nlyr(copernicus_temperature)
)

print(copernicus_time_summary)

```
